answer.answer: The retained passages support limited propositions about Gatecoin’s customer relationships and consent classifications. They do not by themselves establish how a Product Provider under 26EC22 must structure ownership records or demonstrate compliance. Any transfer requires additional legal and factual premises concerning the Product Provider’s terms, role, records, applicable SFC requirements and the relevant assessment interval.

claims.proposition: For customers governed by the 2018 terms, cryptocurrencies were not held on trust; cryptocurrency nevertheless qualifies as property capable of being held on trust, with an exception for NCCs.
claims.status: supported by retained passage; scope limited to Gatecoin’s facts

support.quote: Cryptocurrency is “property” and is capable of being held on trust
Except the Non-Consenting Customers, the 2018 T&C applied to, and governed the relationship between all the Customers
The terms of the 2018 T&C make clear that the cryptocurrencies are not held by Gatecoin on trust for the Customers.

claims.inference: The 2023 judgment treated cryptocurrency as property capable of being held on trust, but concluded that the 2018 terms and objective treatment did not establish a trust for customers other than Non-Consenting Customers (NCCs).
missing_premises: The complete 2023 reasons and evidence for the customer-specific classifications have not been independently rechecked here.
The Product Provider’s contractual terms, custody structure and treatment of assets are not supplied.

claims.proposition: A claimed ownership or trust relationship depends on objectively assessed terms and facts, not terminology alone.
claims.status: supported legal reasoning, but transfer to another arrangement is unresolved

support.quote: the question whether B has a proprietary interest in the property acquired by A for B’s account depends upon their mutual intention, to be ascertained by an objective assessment of the terms of the agreement or relationship
The words used by the parties such as ‘trust’, ‘custody’, ‘belonging’, ‘ownership’, ‘title’, may be persuasive, but they are not conclusive

claims.inference: The court used an objective assessment of the agreement or relationship and surrounding facts; labels such as trust, custody, ownership or title are persuasive but not conclusive.
missing_premises: The full contractual and factual record for any proposed Product Provider arrangement must be examined.
The applicable governing law and any regulatory conditions affecting the arrangement must be identified.

claims.proposition: The 2025 decision supports customer-specific consent classification rather than a universal rule based solely on ledger entries.

support.quote: Cryptocurrency is property and is capable of being held on trust; With the exception of the Non-consenting Customers ... the 2018 T&C applied
The transactions described in the 1st to 4th scenarios did not involve the customers to have accessed or used the Platform.

The transactions described in the 5th to 6th scenarios ... prima facie, the customers fall outside the definition of NCC. However, if the customers are able to prove that they gave the instruction ... before the Relevant Date or without using the Platform, they should be regarded as NCCs.

claims.inference: The 2025 judgment records the 2023 ownership conclusions and applies a fact-sensitive classification of customer consent, distinguishing transactions that did not require platform access from transactions that prima facie did.
missing_premises: The complete 2025 judgment and procedural context remain only partially represented by selected passages.
The evidence available for each proposed customer or transaction is not supplied.

claims.proposition: The 2025 judgment recognises a pooled beneficial interest for qualifying NCCs while treating Mr Samara’s claim as unsecured on the stated facts.
claims.status: supported for the judgment’s stated parties and facts

support.quote: Each NCC is a beneficial tenant-in-common in a pool of cryptocurrency and fiat currency.
Gatecoin does not hold the Subject Bitcoins or the Specified Account on trust for Mr Samara.
Mr Samara is only an unsecured creditor

claims.inference: The 2025 disposition states that NCCs held beneficial tenant-in-common interests in pooled cryptocurrency and fiat currency and specifies different remedies depending on pool shortfall; it also rejects the claimed trust for Mr Samara.
missing_premises: These conclusions concern Gatecoin’s insolvency administration and cannot be assumed to govern a Product Provider’s tokenisation arrangement.
The Product Provider’s pooling, allocation and insolvency arrangements are unknown.

claims.proposition: Gatecoin is at most an analogy or factual comparator; it does not itself establish fulfillment of paragraphs 10, 11 or 14 of 26EC22.
claims.status: deduction from the retained materials; legal correctness not established

support.quote: Product Providers should remain and be ultimately responsible for the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement adopted and record keeping of ownership, regardless of any outsourcing arrangement
Product Providers should ensure that proper records of token holders’ ownership interests in the product are maintained
the ownership representation of the tokens (eg, legal and beneficial title of the tokens, ownership of / interests in the product)

claims.inference: The Gatecoin propositions cannot be transferred automatically to a Product Provider under 26EC22. Transfer would require showing that the Product Provider’s contractual and operational relationship is materially analogous, identifying the applicable ownership representation and governing law, and proving the relevant records and controls.
missing_premises: 26EC22 applicability to the entity, product, activity and interval.
Product Provider status and the precise tokenisation, custody and ledger arrangements.
Terms governing legal and beneficial ownership, settlement finality, reconciliation, transfers, and insolvency treatment.
Evidence that ownership records are complete, accurate, reconciled and maintained through outsourcing.
Any SFC request, applicable demonstration standard and evidence sufficient to satisfy the SFC.

claims.proposition: Operational evidence must be assessed against the applicable standard and full factual record; duty applicability alone does not prove fulfillment.
claims.status: unsupported as a conclusive proposition; additional premises required

support.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction
whether there are regular reconciliations between the records for the extrinsic rights and the records for the distributed ledger tokens

claims.inference: A recorded supervision event or reconciliation would be evidence relevant to paragraphs 10–14, but the retained text does not make either event conclusive of adequate supervision, proper records or SFC satisfaction.
missing_premises: The governing standard for adequacy and materiality.
Scope, frequency, independence, exceptions and remediation of supervision or reconciliation.
Evidence connecting the event to the relevant product, customers, period and ownership interests.

claims.proposition: No complete claim about subsequent treatment of either Gatecoin judgment should be made from this corpus alone.

support.quote: Complete subsequent treatment
Complete subsequent treatment

claims.inference: The retained materials leave later treatment unresolved: one treatment record marks the 2023 decision as followed by the 2025 decision, while the case records also identify complete subsequent treatment as unverified.
missing_premises: A comprehensive survey of subsequent decisions, appeals, or other treatment.
Verification of the relationship between the selected passages and any later authority.

claims.proposition: The scenario-seven treatment cannot safely be converted into an executable classifier without reconciliation of the selected passages.

support.quote: The transactions described in the 7th scenario did not exist and the customers should not be regarded as NCC.
The 5th to 7th scenarios prima facie fall outside the definition of NCC
The following categories of automated transactions ... be treated as having taken place automatically without a customer ... physically access[ing] the Gatecoin platform

claims.inference: There is an unresolved textual tension in the 2025 materials: paragraph 8 says the seventh scenario did not exist, while paragraph 95 groups scenarios five to seven in a prima facie classification statement and the annexure supplies its own operative categories.
missing_premises: The full text, paragraph cross-references and procedural explanation needed to harmonise the passages.
A judicial or authoritative explanation resolving whether paragraph 95’s reference to scenario seven is conditional, inherited or clerical.

rival_readings: The 2025 paragraph-95 grouping may be read as a broad prima facie rule covering scenarios five to seven, subject to proof of non-use or pre-date instructions.

Paragraph 8 may instead be read as controlling the factual finding that scenario seven was not a real category, making paragraph 95’s reference to scenario seven conditional, inherited or otherwise requiring correction.

The Gatecoin trust analysis may provide an analogy for objectively assessing Product Provider terms, but it may not transfer because 26EC22 imposes regulatory responsibilities and SFC-facing standards beyond private-law trust classification.
unresolved: Whether the selected Gatecoin passages accurately capture the complete holdings and ratio after reviewing the full judgments.
Whether any later authority followed, limited, distinguished or overruled the decisions.
The exact Product Provider terms, ownership model, records, reconciliations, outsourcing controls and applicable SFC requests.
The legal standard for demonstrating compliance and obtaining SFC satisfaction under paragraph 14 and footnote 5.
How the scenario-seven passages in the 2025 decision should be harmonised.
